Gut microbiome dysbiosis and associated metabolome changes in tuberculosis patients resolve partially post-therapy
abstractText: Abstract Background Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection in the host and subsequent treatment with anti-tuberculosis drugs impact lung pathophysiology and influence the lung and gut microbiome. Elucidating the role of the gut microbiome and its metabolites in the perturbed metabolic and immune functions observed in tuberculosis (TB) might help design corrective prebiotic and probiotic mixtures. Methodology In this study, fecal samples ( n = 107) of drug-naïve active TB patients (ATB) and controls (other respiratory disease: NTB and healthy) from the two clinical sites were analyzed for microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing), metabolites (GC-TOF-MS), and their correlation. In addition, a longitudinal follow-up study was conducted to understand the dynamics of the microbiota and metabolites during anti-TB treatment in a small cohort ( n = 10). Results Gut microbiota showed site-specificity; however, an overall reduction in alpha diversity was observed in disease states compared with healthy subjects. Underrepresentation of gut commensals ( Faecalibacterium , Ligilactobacillus and Romboustia ) and overrepresentation of Thomasclavelia and Clostridioides were observed among active TB patients. The longitudinally followed-up ATB subjects undergoing treatment showed a time-dependent increase in beta-diversity variance. Over time, the beta diversity of follow-up subjects was almost similar to that of healthy controls. Decrease in the abundance of Streptococcus occurred after anti-TB treatment, with higher levels of opportunistic pathogens, such as Escherichia and Stenotrophomonas . Similarly, specific fecal metabolites also returned to pretreatment levels in relative abundance at later time points. Conclusions The gut microbiota of TB patients showed dysbiosis at the time of case presentation and partially resolved upon complete therapeutic interventions. Partial recovery of microbiota observed during treatment is also reflected in the fecal metabolome, indicating the possible use of microbiome and metabolites as adjunct therapeutics in TB.

title: Postpartum intrusions are associated with child and maternal mental health
abstractText: Abstract Intrusive thoughts of infant-related harm are a common postpartum experience, yet their relationship with maternal and infant mental health is understudied. The current analyses utilized data from 267 participants ( M = 32.2, SD = 4.6) across Australia, the UK, and the US who took part in the COVID-19 Risks Across the Lifespan (CORAL) study. The included participants were pregnant at Time 1 (May to September 2020) and completed measures of postpartum intrusions and mental health at 1–3 follow-up timepoints (up to April 2022) after giving birth. Postpartum intrusions were cross-sectionally associated with poorer maternal (anxiety and depression) and infant (negative affectivity) mental health at Time 4 (~ 1.5 years after Time 1). These associations held when controlling for covariates including antenatal stress, antenatal depression and anxiety, and infant age. Postpartum intrusions were also prospectively associated with infant negative affectivity at Time 4, as well as maternal anxiety and depression at Time 4. These findings highlight the importance of preparing expectant parents for, and further educating antenatal healthcare professionals about, the experience of postpartum intrusions.

title: Ensemble forecasting of ERCOT efficiency and residual price variability using GFDL-CM4 climate projections
abstractText: This paper investigates the climate-induced reliability issues within the Texas ERCOT grid by developing a multi-phase ensemble learning forecasting infrastructure. Meteorological variable forecasts from the CMIP6 GFDL-CM4 climate model were synthesized to project operational efficiency and resulting electricity price fluctuations from 2025 to 2050. Random forest regression and a hybrid SARIMA-XGBoost structure were used to estimate power plant generation and corresponding fuel consumption across seven major energy sources, achieving tolerance accuracies up to 93.7%. Renewables were projected with the most severe efficiency deficits, with wind and solar averaging 8.14% and 12.44% per month, respectively, over the forecasting range. A supporting Gaussian process model directly trained on the projected efficiencies and estimated long-term losses of $29.8 billion for residential consumers and $31.4 billion for retail energy providers under moderate conditions. Risk analysis identified key vulnerable climate zones and dominant predictive weather variables, namely heat-related metrics. Mitigation recommendations were developed based on model outputs, including the deployment of resilient technologies (e.g., anti-icing systems, perovskite PVs, etc.), integrated energy storage, and time-of-use pricing mechanisms. This paper is the first of a multi-part series, with future work extending current data for outage modeling and nonlinear optimization of resilience investment.

title: Targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa ventilator-associated pneumonia with a non-antibiotic and biofilm-disrupting live biotherapeutic: preclinical safety and efficacy study
abstractText: Abstract Background. Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is the second most common hospital-acquired infection and is associated with high morbidity and mortality. The insertion of the endotracheal tube (ETT) compromises the host’s bronchial defenses and facilitates the formation of microbial biofilms and VAP. Although antibiotics remain the cornerstone treatment, their efficacy is often compromised by poor biofilm penetration and the prevalence of multidrug-resistant bacteria. This reveals the need to develop novel non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies. We engineered a non-pathogenic strain of the pulmonary bacteria Mycoplasma pneumoniae CV2 to express anti-biofilm and bactericidal enzymes (VAP platform). The therapeutic effect was validated in a murine model of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection and ex vivo in ETTs of patients with P. aeruginosa -induced VAP. Methods. We evaluated the safety of an improved version of CV2 (CV8, Mycochassis) in a miniature pig model, and its efficacy with the VAP therapeutic platform (CV8_VAP) in a piglet model of P. aeruginosa -induced VAP. CV8_VAP was administered via intralobe instillation or nebulization. We assessed the platform’s ability to degrade biofilms formed on ETTs in vivo and its impact on the airway microbiota. We evaluated bacterial load in the lungs, inflammatory responses, histopathological and the clinical outcomes to provide a comprehensive characterization of therapeutic efficacy and safety. Findings. VAP platform reduced biofilm thickness and P. aeruginosa load in ETTs and lungs, with the nebulized route showing enhanced efficacy. CV8_VAP contributed on microbiome diversity restoration. Inflammatory markers in the lung were markedly decreased, suggesting a local immunomodulatory effect. Interpretation. These findings support that CV8_VAP as a promising, non-antibiotic therapeutic strategy for treating VAP caused by P. aeruginosa . Funding. The project that gave rise to these results has received funding from “La Caixa” Foundation (HR18-00058), and the European Research Council under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation program (670216).

Displacements of large telescope sub-reflector based on 3D laser scanning
abstractText: Abstract The sub-reflector of large-aperture radio telescopes is subject to gravitational deformation and displacement, posing challenges for accurate and rapid monitoring. In this study, a three-dimensional (3D) laser scanning technique was employed to monitor The sub-reflector of a 70-meter radio antenna. Spherical target markers were strategically placed within the feed source cabin to facilitate precise measurements. Rapid data acquisition and analysis enabled determination of the relative positional relationship between the centers of gravity of the target markers and that of The sub-reflector at various elevation angles. A corresponding fitting function was derived, and finite element simulations were conducted for comparison, demonstrating strong agreement between simulation and experimental results. This method was subsequently applied to correct sub-reflector displacements at different elevation angles, ensuring that the antenna gain and efficiency conformed to design specifications and operational requirements. Compared with conventional techniques, the proposed approach offers significantly improved measurement speed and data-processing efficiency.

title: ShapeUpLMD: Automated spatial optimization of laser microdissection for tissue sampling
abstractText: Abstract Laser microdissection (LMD) enables enrichment of defined cellular populations from heterogeneous tissues, providing histologically-resolved molecular profiles with spatial resolution. However, the absence of standardized methods for generating optimized regions of interest (ROIs) limits reproducibility and scalability for spatial multi-omic workflows. To address this gap, we developed ShapeUpLMD, an open-source software tool and integrated workflow that automates the optimization of spatially defined ROIs for LMD, directly from digital pathology annotations. Fresh-frozen uterine serous carcinoma (USC) tumors (n = 11) were sectioned onto polyethylene naphthalate slides, scanned and subsequently annotated by an expert pathologist. Tumor and non-tumor ROIs were used to train tumor-specific classifiers in HALO (Indica Labs). Classified tumor or unbiased whole tissue ROIs were refined and optimized by ShapeUpLMD prior to automated collection on a Leica LMD7 microscope. Across the cohort, predicted tumor ROIs increased effective tumor purity by 86 ± 6% relative to whole tissue while maintaining high spatial concordance between predicted and collected ROIs (accuracy = 0.9 ± 0.05). Data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry quantified upwards of ∼6,500 proteins across spatially resolved ROIs, revealing regionally coherent clustering of adjacent tumor regions and abundance patterns consistent with tumor and non-tumor cell admixture in an unbiased spatial proteomic application. ShapeUpLMD provides an automated, reproducible, and scalable framework that bridges digital pathology with LMD enabling high-fidelity spatial enrichment for multi-omic analyses. This workflow increases throughput, reduces inter-operator variability, and supports standardized, regionally resolved tissue collection for spatial systems biology applications. The software is available at https://github.com/GYNCOE/ShapeUpLMD .

title: Saddlepoint Approximation to the Distribution of the Absorption Time of the Diffusion under Resetting and Reflection
abstractText: Abstract This article provides the saddlepoint approximations to the density and the upper tail probabilities of the first passage time to the null level of the drifted Wiener diffusion, bounded by an upper hard-wall barrier and subject to resetting at the initial value occurring at Poisson times. The proposed saddlepoint approximation is compared with Monte Carlo and with an alternative method of Laplace transform inversion based on the Padé approximation, which likewise possesses the advantage of being expressible in closed-form. These comparisons illustrate the high accuracy of the saddlepoint approximation, in particular in terms of relative errors and for small upper tail probabilities. This high level of accuracy is achieved with a computational cost that is substantially lower than that of its competing methods. The overall conclusion is that, although no universally optimal procedure for the inversion of Laplace transforms can be identified, the saddlepoint method, when applicable (i.e., when a steepness condition on the Laplace transform is satisfied), is one of the most advantageous techniques for Laplace transform inversion.

Numerical simulation of water-sediment two-phase erosion in a split-frame aqueduct and comparison of pier geometry schemes
abstractText: Abstract To address the reduction in structural strength and the decreased safety of separated-type aqueduct bodies due to erosion damage caused by sediment-laden flow, an erosion damage model for the aqueduct structure was established based on the theory of water-sediment two-phase flow erosion damage. This model incorporates the RNG k-ε turbulence model and the Discrete Phase Model (DPM). The FLUENT software was employed to simulate and analyze the erosive damage effects of sediment-laden flow on the separated-type aqueduct under various operating conditions. Additionally, the influence of pier heads with different aspect ratios on the flow field at the aqueduct inlet and outlet was simulated. The results indicate that the unsteady flow characteristics at different locations of the aqueduct and the geometric discontinuities in the aqueduct structure are key factors influencing erosion damage. The erosion damage rate of the structure is positively correlated with flow discharge, sediment concentration, and particle size. Specifically, variations in the frequency and intensity of sediment particle impacts on the wall can exacerbate the erosion damage. The aspect ratio and shape of the separated-type pier heads at the aqueduct inlet and outlet significantly affect the flow pattern. Compared to the common semi-circular inlet and outlet piers, when the aspect ratio of the pier head is in the range of 1.5–2.0 and the shape is streamlined, it can effectively improve the flow pattern at the aqueduct inlet and outlet sections, mitigate the flow-blocking effect of vortices, and significantly reduce the erosion damage rate of the aqueduct. The research findings can provide a technical reference for the optimal design of separated-type aqueducts and the enhancement of their erosion resistance.

title: Sorbates from 1,1-Dialkylsubstituted Alkenes and 3-Haloacrylic Esters via Pd(II)-Isohypsic Catalysis: Focus on Terpenes
abstractText: Abstract Limonene and other 1,1-dialkylsubstituted alkenes undergo a regioselective Pd(II)-catalyzed C–H/C–X coupling with (E) and (Z)-3-bromoacrylates affording 4,4-disubstituted sorbate derivatives as mixtures of geometrical isomers (16 examples). This coupling, unknown to date for the synthesis of 1,3-dienes, follows a mechanism distinct from the well-known Mizoroki–Heck, and works where the Mizoroki–Heck fails. Density functional theory (DFT) computations allowed to propose a plausible mechanism for this transformation.

title: Comparative effects of SMS, phone call and combined mHealth interventions on tuberculosis knowledge among DOTS patients in Lagos, Nigeria
abstractText: Abstract Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, where poor treatment adherence and inadequate patient knowledge continue to contribute to adverse treatment outcomes and multidrug-resistant TB. Patient knowledge is a key upstream determinant of treatment outcomes, yet scalable strategies for improving TB knowledge in low-resource settings remain limited. This study evaluated the comparative and combined effectiveness of SMS and phone-call mHealth interventions on TB knowledge among patients undergoing Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course (DOTS) therapy in Lagos State, Nigeria. Methods A quasi-experimental longitudinal study was conducted across 12 DOTS centres in four local government areas. A total of 128 adults with laboratory-confirmed TB were allocated to four arms: SMS only, phone-call only, combined SMS and phone-call, and standard care (control), with 32 participants per arm. TB knowledge was assessed at baseline, 6th week, and 12th week. Data were analysed using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) with a binomial distribution and logit link, adjusting for age category and education level. A secondary analysis examined the association between TB knowledge and medication adherence using Spearman rank correlations and a separate GEE model. Results Zero attrition was recorded. Phone-call interventions produced the largest knowledge gains (OR = 9.24, 95% CI: 4.07–20.99, p < 0.001), followed by SMS (OR = 3.67, 95% CI: 1.63–8.27, p = 0.002). The combined SMS-plus-phone-call intervention showed no significant benefit over standard care (OR = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.29–1.29, p = 0.197), with estimated marginal means below those of the control group. Significant knowledge gains emerged only at 12-week follow-up (OR = 2.38, p = 0.001), not at midline. The knowledge - adherence correlation attenuated from significant at baseline (rs = 0.326, p < 0.001) and midline (rs = 0.267, p = 0.002) to non-significant at follow-up (rs = 0.066, p = 0.457). Conclusion Phone-call and SMS interventions significantly improved TB knowledge, with phone-calls demonstrating superior effectiveness. Contrary to expectations, combining both modalities conferred no benefit over standard care, suggesting that communication quality and channel appropriateness outweigh message volume. TB programmes should prioritize interactive voice-based follow-up and use SMS as a scalable alternative, while avoiding the uncritical combination of multiple communication channels.

title: A Charge-Consistent Long-Range Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Compatible with Quantum Linear System Algorithms
abstractText: Abstract Charge equilibration in machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) requires repeatedly solving linear systems, providing a promising target for quantum linear-system algorithms (QLSAs). However, conventional electronegativity equalization schemes suffer from spurious fractional charges between neutral fragments at large separations. To address this limitation, we incorporate atom-condensed Kohn–Sham density functional theory approximated to second order (ACKS2) into a long-range equivariant neural-network MLIP. Across benchmark systems, the ACKS2-based model improves energy, force, and charge predictions. At a molecule–metal interface, ACKS2 restores molecular fragments to near-neutral charge states upon separation while preserving local charge redistribution near adsorption. Because ACKS2 charge equilibration reduces to solving a linear system, the classical solver can be directly replaced with the Harrow–Hassidim–Lloyd algorithm during inference, demonstrating compatibility with quantum linear-system solvers. These results indicate that ACKS2 provides a promising framework for charge-aware MLIPs and highlight a potential pathway toward atomistic simulations based on QLSAs.

title: Probable post-traumatic stress disorder after miscarriage: psychological, social, and healthcare-related factors in a mixed-methods study
abstractText: Abstract Background: Miscarriage is commonly managed as a short-term obstetric condition, yet its psychological consequences may extend beyond physical recovery. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of probable post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) after miscarriage and to examine psychological, social, and healthcare-related factors shaping PTSD symptom severity and recovery experiences. Methods: A theory-informed sequential mixed-methods study was conducted at the Post Abortion Care clinic of a tertiary Grade-A women’s and children’s hospital in Sichuan Province, China. In the quantitative phase, 293 women who had experienced miscarriage before 20 completed weeks of gestation completed a digital survey assessing PTSD symptoms, psychological resilience, perceived social support, rumination, coping style, distress disclosure, self-efficacy, anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic growth. Probable PTSD was defined as a Post-traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist–Civilian Version score of 38 or higher. Between-group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and hierarchical multivariable linear regression models were used. In the qualitative phase, nine women participated in semi-structured interviews, which were analyzed thematically and integrated with quantitative findings. Results: The mean PCL-C score was 33.5 ± 12.1, and 95 women (32.4%) screened positive for probable PTSD. Women with probable PTSD had lower psychological resilience than those without probable PTSD (55.4 ± 12.7 vs. 66.4 ± 16.4) and lower perceived social support (59.3 ± 14.0 vs. 66.3 ± 13.8). Higher resilience and perceived social support were associated with lower PTSD symptom severity, while intrusive rumination showed the strongest positive association. Hierarchical regression showed that sociodemographic and reproductive variables alone explained little variance in PTSD symptom severity (adjusted R² = 0.007), whereas adding healthcare-related, psychosocial, and psychological process variables increased explanatory power (adjusted R² = 0.161 and 0.538). Qualitative interviews identified four themes: self-regulation after miscarriage, partner and family support, social safety and stigma, and healthcare communication and care-process burden. These findings contextualized the quantitative associations and highlighted modifiable family, social, and health-service factors. Conclusions: Probable PTSD was common after miscarriage and was shaped by more than individual psychological vulnerability. Post-miscarriage care should move beyond procedure-centered management toward trauma-informed, partner- and family-sensitive, and patient-centered support that includes psychological screening, clear communication, stigma reduction, and attention to care-process burden.

title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
abstractText: Abstract Solution-processed thin films of colloidal lead halide perovskite (LHP) nanocrystals (NCs) show great potential for next-generation optoelectronic devices. However, these NC solids exhibit non-negligible size and shape polydispersity, which introduces both structural and energetic disorder. Here we resolve the exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy to elucidate the impact of disorder on exciton transport. We show that the disorder depends sensitively on the alkylamine ligand used in the synthesis. While shorter alkyl chain lengths lead to high polydispersity, longer alkyl chains lead to a narrower size distribution and smaller particles where quantum confinement becomes more pronounced, consequently leading to increased energetic disorder. Strikingly, we find that exciton transport is less efficient in NC solids with long alkyl chains, despite the fact that they have significantly more narrowly size-distributed ensembles. This demonstrates that energetic disorder rather than structural disorder is the dominant factor for predicting exciton transport within these disordered systems.

Engineering the Band Structure of Ag-Modified Bi2– x WO6 with Bi Vacancies Enhances the Photocatalytic Activity and High Selectivity of CO2 Reduction to CH4
abstractText: Abstract The development of efficient photocatalysts to convert carbon dioxide into renewable fuels is crucial for mitigating the greenhouse effect and addressing the energy crisis. However, the slow migration rate of photogenerated charge carriers remains one of the main factors limiting the efficiency of this process. In this study, we successfully fabricated a Mott–Schottky-type Ag/Bi2–xWO6 heterostructured photocatalyst by in situ growth of Ag nanoparticles on Bi2WO6 substrates containing bismuth vacancies (Bi2–xWO6), thereby increasing the photocatalytic reduction efficiency of CO2. The flower-like morphology of Bi2–xWO6 provides abundant active sites, while the Bi vacancies facilitate CO2 adsorption on the material. Furthermore, after loading with Ag nanoparticles, an Ag/Bi2WO6 Mott–Schottky junction forms at the interface, enabling electrons from the conduction band of Bi2–xWO6 to transfer to the Ag nanoparticles, thus lowering the recombination rate of photogenerated electrons and holes. Overall, the Ag/Bi2–xWO6 heterostructure exhibits excellent photocatalytic activity for CO2 reduction. Notably, compared with those of pure Bi2WO6, the CO/CH4 generation rates of 30Ag/Bi2–xWO6 reached 17.7/13.7 μmol g–1·h–1, and the total electron consumption rate (Relectron) exhibited a 17.54-fold increase. This work provides a paradigm for designing Ag-modified and bismuth vacancy-based photocatalysts for solar-driven CO2 reduction.

title: Latent profile analysis of the nursing work environment and their association with second victim experiences among nurses: a multicentre study in China
abstractText: Abstract Background Nurses involved in adverse events can become “second victims”, but little is known about how the broader nursing work environment is configured and how those configurations relate to second-victim experiences. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of the nursing work environment among Chinese clinical nurses and to examine how profile membership was associated with second-victim distress, perceived support, turnover intention, and absenteeism. Methods Between June and September 2025, 3,309 clinical nurses from 20 tertiary hospitals across three regions in China (Chongqing, Guizhou, and Hong Kong) completed an online survey comprising the Second Victim Experience and Support Tool (SVEST) and the Nursing Work Environment Scale. Latent profile analysis was used to identify distinct subgroups, and multinomial logistic regression was performed to examine factors associated with profile membership. Results Three latent profiles were identified: Moderately Resourced (74.7%), Support-Deprived (9.4%), and Optimally Supported (15.9%). Relative to the Support-Deprived profile, supervisor support showed the strongest association with Optimally Supported membership (OR = 0.14), followed by institutional (OR = 0.19) and colleague support (OR = 0.50). The Support-Deprived group had the highest rate of adverse event exposure yet the lowest perceived support, whereas psychological distress did not differ across profiles. The three-profile structure was largely consistent across regions, with only a small difference in the prevalence of the Support-Deprived profile (highest in Hong Kong, 11.4%). Two hypothesis-generating concepts—permissive absence and structural–relational asymmetry—are proposed for future testing. Conclusion The nursing work environment was significantly associated with second victim experiences. A small but clinically vulnerable Support-Deprived subgroup warrants proactive, organisation-level intervention, and context-tailored strategies should complement rather than replace system-wide efforts to improve the practice environment.

title: Doppler-based GNSS variometry for velocity estimation in high-dynamic sounding rocket missions
abstractText: Abstract This work investigates the application of GNSS variometry for onboard velocity estimation in sounding rocket flights, with particular focus on the use of Doppler observations under high-dynamic conditions. The study assesses, for the first time, the performance of a variometric algorithm originally developed for geodetic applications based on carrier-phase observations, here extended to Doppler observables in a high-dynamic aerospace scenario. The analysis is based on data acquired during two sounding rocket launch campaigns conducted in Roccaraso, Italy (May 2025), and Texas, USA (June 2025), using a lightweight Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) payload composed of a Raspberry Pi single-board computer and dual u-blox ZED-F9P chipsets. Observations from GPS, Galileo, and BeiDou constellations on the L1 frequency were recorded simultaneously at different sampling rates, allowing a comparative evaluation of observation continuity and the corresponding variometric velocity solutions under both nominal and anomalous flight conditions. The results show that carrier-phase variometry, although associated with lower nominal uncertainty, is severely affected during the boost phase, where strong accelerations lead to degraded observation quality and incomplete reconstruction of the velocity peak. Doppler observations, by contrast, maintain continuity throughout all flight phases including the most demanding ones, and yield velocity estimates capable of reproducing the main features of the flight profile. Within the limitations of the available experimental dataset, the analysis suggests that Doppler-based variometry represents a robust and practically viable approach for GNSS velocity estimation in sounding rocket applications when carrier-phase continuity or integrity is reduced.

title: Enhanced OER kinetics with NiFeLa LDH electrocatalysts supported onto Ta-doped SnO2
abstractText: The direct synthesis of a series of NiFeLa-layered double hydroxides (LDH) supported on Ta-doped SnO2 (LDH@SnO2) was carried out at various loadings (15, 33 and 67 wt%). These materials provided enhanced oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics in alkaline medium with Tafel slope values of 94.6 mV/dec and 130.6 mV/dec for 33LDH@SnO2 and 67LDH@SnO2, respectively. In addition, the 33LDH@SnO2 electrocatalytic material provided greater performance than the unsupported NiFeLa-LDH and was selected as anodic catalyst for full cell anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyser testing. The AEM water electrolysis cell provided a current density of 603 mA/cm2 with no performance decay after 24 h at 2.0V, thus indicatin its potential applicability in larger scale systems.

Influence of spreader dispersion on rumour propagation in complex networks
abstractText: Abstract In social systems, information and misinformation can enter the underlying interaction network through multiple independent sources. Its cumulative reach depends not only on the influence of the sources but also on how they are collectively positioned in the network. Here, we study how the spatial dispersion of multiple initial spreaders influences rumour propagation on complex networks. This setting differs from epidemic spreading because rumour spreaders may become inactive after contacting already informed nodes. Hence, the placement of the initial spreaders affects not only initial coverage but also the timing of deactivation. We consider classical three-state rumour dynamics with interaction-driven stifling and compare dispersion-based initial spreader selection strategies, constructed using farthest-first traversal and a hybrid local-connectivity refinement, with non-dispersion-based strategies. Numerical simulations on Erd\"{o}s-R\'{e}nyi, Barab\'{a}si-Albert and Watts-Strogatz networks, together with six real-world network datasets, show that dispersed initial spreaders generally increase both the final rumour size and the peak fraction of active spreaders. This occurs because dispersion reduces overlap among spreading regions and delays deactivation caused by contacts with already informed nodes. The hybrid strategy, which combines topological separation with local connectivity, typically outperforms degree-based seeding over a broad range of spreading and stifling probabilities. Our results show that in multi-source rumour spreading, a combination of broad separation between the initial spreaders and strong local connectivity is crucial for maximizing rumour reach and intensity.

title: Metabolic–clinical subtypes predict survival in BCLC-C hepatocellular carcinoma receiving synchronous TACE plus targeted and immunotherapy
abstractText: Abstract Background The synchronous combination of TACE, TKIs, and ICIs has improved outcomes for patients with BCLC-C HCC, yet treatment response varies widely. This study aimed to identify metabolically distinct phenotypes that predict response to synchronous triple therapy. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1,792 patients with BCLC-C HCC. Propensity score matching and L2-penalized multivariate Cox regression were performed, followed by XGBoost with SHAP transformation and K-means clustering to define metabolic subtypes. Subgroup analyses with interaction testing were conducted across clinical strata to validate the robustness of the clustering system. Results After propensity score matching (716 pairs), synchronous triple therapy significantly improved overall survival compared with pre-immunotherapy TACE (median, 28.0 vs. 8.0 months; P < 0.001). Eight metabolic and clinical factors (AFP, TP, GGT, LDH, P, metastasis, HCO3, RBC) were identified as independent predictors. K-means clustering resolved four distinct metabolic phenotypes: metabolically fit (Cluster 1, 58.5%), metabolically compensated (Cluster 2, 24.6%), tumor-metabolism dominant (Cluster 3, 14.5%), and metabolically exhausted (Cluster 4, 2.4%). The metabolically fit phenotype demonstrated exceptional survival (median OS, 38.0 months; 1-year OS, 82.7%), while the metabolically exhausted phenotype showed a dismal prognosis (median OS, 4.0 months; 1-year OS, 4.2%). Subgroup analyses confirmed that the favorable prognosis of the metabolically fit phenotype remained consistent across all clinical strata. Conclusions The metabolic fitness-based clustering framework identifies patients with BCLC-C HCC most likely to benefit from synchronous triple therapy, suggesting that routine laboratory tests may help guide precision patient selection.

title: Queen brood care behavior is plastic and socially regulated in an annually eusocial insect
abstractText: Abstract The ability of organisms to shift behaviors in response to their environment, known as behavioral plasticity, is a key facet of survival in many environmental contexts. Organisms living in social groups additionally exhibit behavioral plasticity with changes to the social environment. In eusocial insects, queens often transition away from brood care toward reproductive specialization as workers assume caregiving responsibilities. However, the extent to which queens retain behavioral plasticity following this transition varies among eusocial insects and remains poorly understood in bumble bees. In this study, we examined plasticity in bumble bee queen brood care in response to total worker loss, specifically exploring two key behaviors: feeding and incubation. We further asked whether queens become less plastic across colony development​ stages by examining colonies at ​early, middle, later​, and ultimately mature developmental stages. We found that across all nest developmental stages explored, queens retained their ability to perform brood care. Further, we found that queens regulate feeding and incubation behaviors differently, displaying a greater plasticity in incubation than in feeding following changes in social conditions. Broadly, this work highlights how life-history transitions do not necessarily mark the end of an organism’s behavioral plasticity.

title: Gender Equality and Workplace Inclusivity among Employees of a Government Agency in the Philippines
abstractText: Gender equality and workplace inclusivity are essential to fostering fair, respectful, and supportive work environments where employees receive equal opportunities and are encouraged to participate and contribute. This study aimed to determine the perceived levels of gender equality and workplace inclusivity among employees of a Philippine government agency. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed using a census approach involving 40 employees from an identified work unit of the government agency. Descriptive and inferential statistical techniques were used to analyze data collected via a researcher-structured questionnaire. Results showed that employees perceived high levels of gender equality and workplace inclusivity. All six dimension-level Pearson correlations between the gender equality dimensions (equal opportunities and fair treatment) and the workplace inclusivity dimensions (respect and acceptance, participation and involvement, and organizational support) were positive and statistically significant, ranging from r = .615 to r = .862 (p < .001). Although respondents generally perceived limited gaps in workplace policies and practices, areas requiring continuous improvement were identified in accountability and monitoring mechanisms, program evaluation processes, organizational support systems, employee feedback utilization, and safe reporting procedures. Based on these findings, a strategy roadmap for strengthening gender equality and workplace inclusivity was prepared to support the continuous enhancement of gender-responsive and inclusive workplace practices. The findings may serve as a basis for government leaders, human resource managers, and gender and development focal persons in formulating and enhancing evidence-based policies, programs, and interventions that promote gender equality, workplace inclusivity, employee well-being, and organizational effectiveness.

Investigation of Gamma Radiation Effects on the Resistance of Some Types of Lamps in Active Power Mode
abstractText: This study aims to investigate the effects of gamma radiation on some various lamp types while they are operating in active power mode. The gamma radiation can degrade electronic devices, and understanding its influence on the lamp's functionality is critical for applications in high-radiation environments. This research quantifies the radiation resistance thresholds of incandescent, fluorescent, and other lamps. The objectives are to determine the gamma radiation levels lamps can withstand before exhibiting performance declines, identify the physical and chemical changes in the lamp components caused by radiation exposure, and develop strategies to enhance lamp radiation hardness. The methodology utilizes controlled radiation sources Co-60, to expose lamps to increasing dosages while monitoring electrical and photometric parameters. Moreover, materials analysis and integrity assessments will also be conducted. Quantitative performance data will be used to identify vulnerable lamp components and correlations between design factors and radiation resistance. The findings will help guide the development of lighting solutions tailored for high-reliability operation in the presence of gamma radiation. LED bulbs exhibited remarkable resilience to gamma exposure. Only a 5% reduction in luminance was noted at 100 kGy, indicating a high level of radiation hardness. The comparison illustrates that LED bulbs maintain performance closest to control samples, followed by incandescent bulbs. CFLs and OLED panels are more susceptible to gamma radiation-induced degradation.

title: ABO and Rhesus Blood Group Distribution and Frequency among Blood Donors at El-Marj and Al-Bayda Cities in Northeastern of Libya
abstractText: Background: The ABO and Rh blood group antigens are the most predominantly used blood group antigens in clinical services and are utilized to shun transfusion reactiveness and maternal mortalities. The present study aims to determine the frequency and distribution of ABO and Rh (D) in the two cities in northeastern Libya, EL-Marj and Al-Bayda and make a comparison between the two cities according to characteristics of blood groups in each one. Methods: A retrospective study was carried out at the blood banks of two cities in the northeastern of Libya EL-Marj and Al-Bayda by studying all records of the last years, and making comparisons between the two cities. it collected information about 24823 donors from records of blood banks in both cities. Result: the number of the donors that have been studied is 24823 donors. It shows the year 2021 has more frequency for donors 9358 (37.7%). The most frequent ABO blood groups were O, then A (36.4%) and (29.7%), respectively, whereas, the smallest frequent one was AB (8.9 %). As for the rhesus factor, the Rh-positive comprised (84.9%) and the Rh-negative (15.1%) of donors. Conclusions: The current study deduces that the most common blood group is O and the least common is AB among the blood donors at Al-Bayda and EL-Marj cities in Libya. Concerning the Rh blood group system, the Rh-positive donor's proportion was 84.9% and the Rh-negative was 15.1%.

title: Evaluating LDPC Codes for OFDM/QAM Optical Fiber Systems
abstractText: Optical fiber communications are a critical infrastructure for modern data transmission, providing high throughput and exceptional reliability over long distances. However, the integrity of the transmitted data remains vulnerable to distortion, which increase the bit-error-rate (BER). This effectively arises due to the increased dispersion resulted by the increase in the bit rate. Several correction codes have been developed to overcome this limitation, such as Manchester, Reed-Solomon, and Reed-Muller, however most of them suffer from significant drawbacks including high complexity, power consumption, and suboptimal error correction capabilities. The low density parity check (LDPC) code has been introduced as an effective coding technique to overcome the aforementioned limitation due to its attractive features, such as iterative decoding and parallel processing. This paper aims to verify the effectiveness of the LDPC code by applying it side by side with other codes designed for the same purpose on an OFDM/QAM-based optical communications system and comparing the performance. The performance is examined based on BER and constraints using Optisystem software. The results confirmed the superiority of the LDPC code as it shows lower BER, which contributes to increasing the transmission distance.

title: Dose-Dependent Inhibition of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Growth by Thapsigargin: Insights into Antifungal Mechanisms
abstractText: This study explores the inhibitory effects of thapsigargin on the growth of Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Utilizing a dose-response approach, we evaluated the antifungal efficacy of thapsigargin at concentrations ranging from 0.1 mg/mL to 5 mg/mL, incubated over 2 and 4 days. Results demonstrated a significant dose-dependent inhibition of yeast growth, with maximum inhibition observed at 5 mg/mL after 4 days. Specifically, the percentage inhibition was calculated as 63% compared to the control groups, which included ethyl acetate and sterile water. The findings indicate that thapsigargin exerts potent antifungal effects on S. cerevisiae, with potential implications for food safety and fermentation processes. This research fills existing gaps in the literature regarding the effects of plant-derived compounds on beneficial yeast species, contributing valuable insights into natural antifungal strategies. The results underscore the significance of Thapsia garganica as a viable candidate for further exploration in antifungal applications, particularly in the context of food preservation and biotechnological processes.

title: Navigated robotic guidance for minimally invasive bertolotti resection technical feasibility and workflow evaluation
abstractText: Abstract Bertolotti syndrome is characterized by symptomatic lumbosacral transitional vertebral anatomy in which an enlarged transverse process articulates or fuses with the sacrum or ilium. Diagnosis can be difficult because transitional anatomy is common, symptoms may overlap with other spinal disorders, and the pain generator may arise from the pseudoarticulation, adjacent disc or facet, instability, or nerve compression. When targeted nonoperative treatment fails, surgical options include resection, nerve decompression, or fusion depending on anatomy and the dominant pain mechanism. Published evidence supports image guidance for localization and confirmation of resection and describes early robotic assistance for trajectory and incision planning; however, evidence specific to robotic Bertolotti resection remains limited. This article evaluates the feasibility of a preoperatively planned, navigated robotic workflow for minimally invasive Bertolotti resection. A framework is presented for preoperative computed-tomography planning, convergent access through a minimally invasive incision, trajectory-controlled drilling of bone-cut trajectories across the transverse processes and pseudoarticulations, navigated osteotomy, fragment removal and verification of complete decompression or resection. Feasibility was assessed by completion of planned robotic and navigated steps, intraoperative confirmation of registration and resection, and review of technical, perioperative, and imaging outcomes. These concepts may improve reproducibility and reduce challenges related to limited visualization and complex three-dimensional anatomy, but do not prove superior outcomes. This paper outlines a novel technique; however, further comparative studies using standardized measures of pain, disability, operative time, blood loss, radiation exposure, navigation accuracy, resection quality, and reoperation rate are needed before the clinical value of robotic guidance is established.

title: Analisis Implementasi Program Rehabilitasi Sosial pada Anak Berhadapan dengan Hukum (ABH) di UPT Panti Sosial Anak Kalimantan Barat
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendepenelitiankan dan menganalisis implementasi program rehabilitasi sosial pada Anak Berhadapan dengan Hukum (ABH) di UPT Panti Sosial Anak Kalimantan Barat. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode deskriptif. Subjek penelitian meliputi pihak yang terlibat dalam pelaksanaan program rehabilitasi sosial dan ABH yang mengikuti program. Pada periode 2025–2026 terdapat 13 ABH yang menjadi sasaran program, seluruhnya laki-laki. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi serta diuji melalui triangulasi sumber dan teknik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa implementasi program dilaksanakan melalui tiga aspek, yaitu perencanaan, pelaksanaan, dan hasil program. Perencanaan diawali dengan penerimaan anak dan asesmen kebutuhan yang menjadi dasar penyusunan program. Pelaksanaan meliputi bimbingan rohani Islam, tata boga, bimbingan sosial, dan penyuluhan kesehatan dengan dukungan komunikasi, sumber daya, disposisi, dan struktur birokrasi. Hasil program menunjukkan perubahan positif pada sikap dan perilaku, peningkatan pengetahuan dan keterampilan, kemampuan bersosialisasi, serta kesiapan ABH untuk kembali ke keluarga dan masyarakat. Program juga mendukung pemulihan keberfungsian sosial ABH

title: Strategi Personal Branding Mahasiswa FISIP Universitas Malikussaleh di LinkedIn Menuju Karier Profesional
abstractText: Perkembangan teknologi digital mendorong mahasiswa mempersiapkan karier melalui pengelolaan identitas profesional di ruang daring. LinkedIn menyediakan ruang jejaring profesional yang dapat dimanfaatkan untuk memperkenalkan kompetensi dan pengalaman sebelum memasuki dunia kerja. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis strategi personal branding mahasiswa mahasiswa FISIP Universitas Malikussaleh di LinkedIn serta mengkaji proses impression management yang menyertainya. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan pemilihan informan secara purposive sampling, terdiri atas enam mahasiswa angkatan 2022 dan dua informan pendukung dari kalangan alumni. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi tak terstruktur, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui redukasi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa mahasiswa membangun identitas profesional melalui pengelolaan profil, penyajian pengalaman dan konten relevan, konsistensi citra, serta pemanfaatan fitur LinkedIn untuk memperluas jaringan dan visibilitas kompetensi. Dalam perspektif Goffman, profil dan unggahan menjadi fornt stage, sedangkan seleksi pengalaman, penyiapan dokumentasi, dan penyusunan narasi merupakan back stage. Penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa personal branding di LinkedIn merupakan proses seleksi dan penyajian pengalaman nyata secara terencana sebagai bagian dari persiapan karier.

title: Rompiendo ciclos intergeneracionales: Regulación emocional, apego seguro y bienestar infantil desde el enfoque de la Nueva Escuela Mexicana
abstractText: El bienestar emocional en la infancia constituye un factor determinante para el desarrollo integral de las personas, ya que influye en la forma en que los niños aprenden, se relacionan con los demás y enfrentan los desafíos de la vida cotidiana. La salud emocional de los adultos cuidadores incide directamente en la manera en que los niños aprenden a reconocer, expresar y regular sus propias emociones, dado que los menores aprenden principalmente a través de la observación e imitación de las conductas adultas. Cuando los adultos no han desarrollado habilidades de regulación afectiva o arrastran heridas emocionales no resueltas de su propia infancia, tienden a reproducir patrones disfuncionales en la crianza, lo que puede afectar la seguridad emocional y el bienestar de los niños a su cargo. El presente artículo de reflexión analiza la relación entre la salud emocional del adulto y el desarrollo del bienestar en la infancia, a partir de una revisión de la literatura especializada en psicología del desarrollo, teoría del apego y educación emocional. Se examina cómo las heridas emocionales no resueltas tienden a repetirse en la dinámica familiar, generando ciclos intergeneracionales que pueden prevenirse mediante procesos terapéuticos y educación emocional. La evidencia revisada sugiere que el bienestar emocional del adulto constituye una condición necesaria para ofrecer a la infancia entornos seguros y afectivamente nutritivos, lo que favorece la construcción de vínculos seguros y una autoestima saludable.

title: Template Mineralized, Decellularized Matrix-Alginate-Based Bioink Provides Structural Reinforcement in Caprine Ex Vivo Bone Defect Model
abstractText: Abstract Clinical management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) remains a significant surgical problem. Current bioinks fail to support initial loading on bone tissue. In this study, goat-derived decellularized matrix (DCM) was used as a template for controlled mineralization, while alginate improved the printability and cellular viability. DCM proteins acted as a natural template for hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal nucleation and growth, mimicking bone nanocomposite chemistry while enhancing structural reinforcement. HA formation on DCM template was visualized by atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis, characteristic phosphate (PO43–) peaks in attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), and the HA-specific (211) diffraction peak in X-ray diffraction (XRD). Mineralized DCM was blended with alginate to formulate printable bioinks. Rheological analysis showed dominant elastic behavior (G′ > G″), shear-thinning flow, and rapid post-shear recovery. Mechanical testing further demonstrated enhanced compressive strength in HA-DCM-alginate constructs. Bioprinting with osteoblast cells demonstrated higher cellular viability in the mineralized ink while enhancing osteogenic differentiation, via both biochemical and biophysical signaling from the mineralized-DCM ink. In an ex vivo defect model, the HA-DCM-alginate system significantly increased the compressive properties of the defect construct, providing immediate structural reinforcement at the defect site. Overall, the current mineralized bioink can provide both mechanical support and bone regeneration and holds promising potential for surgical application.

Laundering efficiencies of extractors vs household machines on wildland fire contaminants
abstractText: Background Wildland firefighter gear typically consists of shirts and pants manufactured from textiles such as Nomex® and Kevlar. These materials provide a flame resistant barrier to the wearer but may be difficult to clean. Methods Twelve shirts worn in recent wildland fire events in the United States (US) were analyzed to determine contamination, specifically semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs) contamination so that best cleaning practices could be established. Several SVOCs, including phthalates and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), were identified. New Nomex® textiles used to construct wildland shirts and pants were contaminated and laundered under a range of temperature conditions using a commercial extractor at 40-60 °C (105–140oF) and a household machine at 29-49 °C (85–120°F) to determine cleaning efficiency between commercial (extractor) machines and household washers. Key results Results showed high removal rates (typically above 58%) for all of the chemicals using a temperature and g-forces controlled commercial extractor and a front-loading household washer with a cold/warm/hot selector and no g-force control. Conclusions This research suggests that a dedicated household-grade laundering machine may provide cleaning levels equivalent to commercial extractors for wildland gear. Implications The results may provide a new option for cleaning Nomex wildland protective clothing.

abstractText: This study aimed to analyze suicide risk among Indigenous students at the Centro Universitario del Norte (CUNorte) during the 2025-B academic term. A quantitative, nonexperimental, cross-sectional, descriptive study was conducted using a nonprobability purposive sample of 229 Indigenous students enrolled in undergraduate degree and engineering programs at CUNorte. Data were collected using the six-item short version of the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS, 2024), which showed an internal consistency coefficient of α = .871. Data were analyzed using SPSS, version 22. The results showed that 73.8% of participants were classified as having low suicide risk, whereas 26.2% presented moderate or high levels. The mean age was 21.6 years; female participants predominated, and 72.5% were single. Although low suicide risk predominated, a subgroup of students showed psychological vulnerability requiring priority attention. The findings support strengthening institutional prevention strategies, psychological support, and mental health promotion within the university community through an intercultural approach.

Performance-Driven Generative Design for Daylighting Optimization in a Tangerang Aerotropolis Office Building
abstractText: Daylighting in tropical climates may increase glare risk in office buildings. This issue is particularly relevant in the Tangerang Aerotropolis area, where humid tropical conditions and airport operational safety regulations constrain building development. This study optimized daylighting performance in an office building using a Performance-Driven Generative Design approach. The workflow integrated Rhinoceros 3D, Grasshopper, ClimateStudio, and Galapagos to evaluate six envelopes and building mass variables. The optimization evaluated 950 design alternatives across 18 generations using UDI₁₀₀–₃₀₀₀ as the objective function. A maximum UDI₁₀₀–₃₀₀₀ of 95.5% was achieved with a WWR of 0.47, window height of 2.53 m, shading spacing and depth of 0.40 m, building width of 12 m, and orientation of 76°. Best-performing configurations converged within WWR 0.40–0.47, window height 2.50–2.60 m, shading spacing 0.30–0.50 m, shading depth 0.30–0.40 m, building width 12–13 m, and orientation 72°–84°. The results identified a high-performing configuration and recurring parameter ranges among the best-performing solutions.

Adaptive structural fusion for dielectric constant prediction using physics-guided graph neural networks
abstractText: Abstract Accurate prediction of dielectric response is essential for improving the discovery of materials for electronic, energy-storage, radio-frequency, sensing, and optoelectronic applications. However, dielectric datasets are typically dominated by materials with low to moderate dielectric response, while high-dielectric materials are severely under-represented, making reliable prediction across the full property range challenging. This work proposes a physics-guided extension of the Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Network (CGCNN) for total dielectric constant prediction through Adaptive Structural Fusion (ASF). This refines learned atomic representations using five physically motivated local descriptors: coordination number, mean bond length, bond-angle variation, local electronegativity difference, and atomic polarizability. A context-dependent Knowledge-Guided Graph Aggregation (KGGA) module is subsequently evaluated both independently and in combination with ASF to investigate whether adaptive graph aggregation depends on the quality of the underlying node representations. Four controlled architectures -the baseline CGCNN, CGCNN with KGGA, CGCNN with ASF, and the proposed model CGCNN with both ASF and KGGA- were evaluated on an identical frozen split of a curated benchmark containing 5,874 inorganic crystalline materials. Relative to the baseline CGCNN, the proposed framework – CGCNN with both ASF and KGGA- reduced the mean absolute error (MAE) from 11.139 to 8.828, decreased the root mean square error (RMSE) from 53.315 to 42.275, and increased the coefficient of determination (R²) from 0.214 to 0.506, corresponding to approximately 21% reductions in MAE and RMSE. Paired material-level statistical analysis further demonstrated a mean absolute-error reduction of 2.311 (95% bootstrap confidence interval: 0.960–3.736) and lower prediction error for 68.4% of the 588 held-out test materials. Regime-wise evaluation showed that the proposed model achieved the lowest MAE in five of six predefined dielectric regimes, a descriptive observation that should be interpreted cautiously given the sparse high-dielectric test samples. Representative material analysis further illustrated substantial error reductions for selected chemically and structurally diverse inorganic compounds. These results indicate that physics-guided representation refinement and adaptive graph aggregation are complementary strategies for improving dielectric property prediction while highlighting the importance of regime-aware evaluation for long-tailed materials datasets.

Angkasa Lepas Sebagai Dimensi Baharu Ancaman Keselamatan Nasional Malaysia
abstractText: ABSTRAK Kemunculan teknologi angkasa lepas sebagai instrumen strategik dalam era geopolitik moden telah membuka satu dimensi baharu dalam perbincangan mengenai keselamatan nasional. Angkasa lepas kini tidak lagi terbatas kepada misi eksplorasi saintifik semata-mata, sebaliknya telah berkembang menjadi medan persaingan strategik antara negara-negara kuasa besar untuk menguasai keupayaan ketenteraan dari orbit. Bagi Malaysia, kebergantungan yang semakin meningkat terhadap satelit bagi komunikasi, navigasi, pemantauan bencana dan keselamatan sempadan menimbulkan kerentanan baharu yang belum ditangani secara menyeluruh dalam dasar-dasar yang membentuk keselamatan negara. Artikel ini meneliti definisi konseptual keselamatan angkasa yang bukan sahaja menekankan aspek perlindungan aset angkasa lepas tetapi juga kaitannya dengan keselamatan manusia. Kajian ini turut menghuraikan pengklasifikasian bentuk ancaman angkasa yang terbahagi kepada dua kategori utama iaitu ancaman tradisional dan bukan tradisional. Kajian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan pengumpulan data primer melalui analisis dokumen rasmi negara seperti Dasar Pertahanan Negara (DPN), Kertas Putih Pertahanan (KPP), Dasar Angkasa Negara (DAN) serta temubual elit. Data sekunder turut diperoleh daripada buku akademik, artikel jurnal dan laporan berita. Melalui pendekatan ini, dapatan awal kajian menunjukkan bahawa angkasa lepas berpotensi menjadi sumber ancaman kepada negara dan wajar diiktiraf sebagai salah satu persekitaran strategik yang perlu dilindungi serta diurus secara holistik. Kajian ini menekankan keperluan kepada hala tuju dasar yang lebih jelas, perdebatan akademik yang lebih mendalam serta pengintegrasian komprehensif aspek keselamatan angkasa ke dalam kerangka keselamatan nasional Malaysia. Kata kunci: Angkasa Lepas, Strategik, Geopolitik, Kuasa Besar, Keselamatan Nasional ABSTRACT The emergence of space technology as a strategic instrument in the modern geopolitical era has opened a new dimension in discussions on national security. Outer space is no longer confined solely to scientific exploration missions, instead it has evolved into a strategic arena of competition among major powers seeking to dominate military capabilities from orbit. For Malaysia, the growing reliance on satellites for communication, navigation, disaster monitoring and border security introduces new vulnerabilities that have yet to be comprehensively addressed within the country’s national security policy framework. This article examines the conceptual definition of space security, which not only emphasizes the protection of space assets but also its relevance to human security. It further elaborates on the classification of space threats into two main categories, traditional and non-traditional. The study employs a qualitative approach, drawing on primary data through the analysis of official national documents such as the National Defence Policy (DPN), Defence White Paper (KPP), National Space Policy (DAN) as well as elite interviews. Secondary data is also derived from academic books, journal articles and news reports. Through this approach, the preliminary findings indicate that outer space has the potential to become a source of threats to the nation and should be recognized as one of the strategic environments that must be safeguarded while managed holistically. The study underscores the need for clearer policy direction, deeper academic debate and comprehensive integration of space security into Malaysia’s national security framework. Keywords: Outer Space, Strategic, Geopolitics, Great Power, National Security

SARIMA-Based water consumption forecasting for distribution planning and performance evaluation at padang municipal waterworks
abstractText: This study develops a forecasting model for water consumption at the Padang Municipal Waterworks using the Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) approach to enhance water distribution planning. Monthly consumption data from 2007 to 2024 were analyzed using time-series techniques. The results identify SARIMA (1,1,1)(1,1,1)₁₂ as the optimal model, effectively capturing both long-term trends and seasonal fluctuations. The model demonstrates high predictive accuracy with a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 5.26%. While the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 238,967.70 m³ suggests limited robustness against extreme data anomalies, the model remains highly effective for forecasting under normal operational conditions. These findings provide a data-driven foundation for Padang City’s water resource management, offering a more precise tool for anticipating demand cycles. Future research should consider incorporating external variables to better account for non-seasonal volatility.

Mechanism and Kinetics of Nucleation and Growth in Amine Aerosols for Post-Combustion Carbon Capture
abstractText: Abstract As the major component of organic amine emission, amine aerosol can generate the substantial secondary pollutants, posing serious environmental impacts and hindering the large-scale deployment of absorption carbon capture. The existing studies have proposed several end-of-pipe strategies to achieve 99% removal within a reasonable cost range while it is still challenging. It is necessary to elucidate the nucleation and growth mechanisms of amine aerosols. Herein we investigate the mechanism and kinetics of amine nucleation and growth by molecular dynamics simulation, quantum chemistry calculation, and experiment. Molecular dynamics simulation results show that the aerosol nucleation process follows a typical growth pathway characterized by mutual attraction, collision-coalescence, and nucleation. The results show that, compared with the nucleation process without chemical reactions, the reaction energy barrier of the rate-determining step in the nucleation process involving chemical reactions is reduced by 16.56 kJ/mol, reaching 11.55 kJ/mol. The reaction rate of the rate-determining step is 1.214 × 10–9 s–1, which is 3 orders of magnitude higher than that of the nonreactive reaction. This finding is further verified by structural characterization using FTIR experiments. It is expected to provide further mechanistic insights into the removal of amine aerosols.

title: Attributing Chemiluminescence NO2 Measurement Interference to Oxidized Reactive Nitrogen Chemistry in Urban Atmospheres: Its Implications for Photochemical Pollution Assessment
abstractText: Abstract Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a key precursor to ozone and aerosols; therefore, it has been widely monitored in air quality networks using the chemiluminescence (CL) method. However, interference from oxidized nitrogen species (NOz) in CL-based measurements can lead to NO2 overestimation, introducing uncertainty into atmospheric composition assessments. Using 2 years of parallel CL and cavity-attenuated phase shift (CAPS) measurements at an urban Seoul, we quantified mean interference (z* = NO2_CL – NO2_CAPS) of 3.0 ppbv, with larger values in winter than in summer. We developed machine learning models that reproduced z* well (r > 0.7). Explainable AI results indicated that model inference process was broadly consistent with heterogeneous NOz formation in winter and photochemical NOz production in summer. Applying our models to global megacities suggests regime-dependent interference of about 10–20% of reported NO2. This study provides a framework for estimating NOz interference in CL-based NO2 measurements.

abstractText: The increasingly competitive culinary industry requires businesses to improve service quality and manage their digital reputation to influence consumer purchasing decisions. This study aims to examine the effects of service quality and Electronic Word of Mouth (eWOM) on purchasing decisions among consumers of Koka Ramen Express Sudirman, both partially and simultaneously. This research employs a quantitative approach with a causal associative design. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using purposive sampling involving 120 respondents who had previously purchased and consumed products at Koka Ramen Express Sudirman. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics 29. The results indicate that service quality has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.207 and a significance level of less than 0.001. Electronic Word of Mouth also has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.184 and a significance level of less than 0.001. Simultaneously, both variables have a significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a coefficient of determination of 63.6%. Service quality is the more dominant factor influencing purchasing decisions compared to eWOM. These findings imply that management should improve employee friendliness, service speed, and restaurant cleanliness while optimizing social media activities and responding professionally to customer reviews to strengthen consumer confidence in making purchasing decisions.

title: The musculoskeletal phenotype of fatal strychnine poisoning
abstractText: Abstract Background Strychnine poisoning is still a documented entity in forensic medicine. Strychnine is a competitor of the post-synaptic glycine receptors at the level of motor neurons and interneurons in the spinal cord, which blocks glycine inhibitory effects on post-synaptic neurons leading to involuntary muscle contractions. Strychnine poisoning appears with an initial excitability, followed by vomiting, development of convulsions, with muscle contractions, and can result fatal due to spasm of respiratory muscles. Although it is widely accepted that diaphragm and accessory respiratory muscles are primarily responsible of death, the impact of strychnine at the level of skeletal muscle fibers morphology has been poorly investigated, and the literature does not report evidence to understand the precise effect of strychnine on skeletal muscles cytological organization. Indeed, the study of the effects of strychnine and other poisons is challenging because of the heterogeneity of skeletal muscle fibers and their distinct physiological properties, which could determine different responses to each toxic substance. Case presentation We report a suicidal case of a 50-year-old man who died following the ingestion of a lethal dose of strychnine. At the time of the crime scene examination, rigor mortis was present and fully established. A complete post mortem examination was performed few days after death. By the time the body was examined on the autopsy table, rigor mortis had already resolved. This was consistent with the expected evolution of rigor mortis over the interval between the crime scene examination and the autopsy. The autopsy examination revealed enlargement of both lungs with abundant blood-tinged fluid and foam on the main bronchi. From toxicological analyses, it emerged that massive concentrations of strychnine were present in peripheral blood, gastric contents and vitreous humor. To comprehend the impact of strychnine poisoning to respiratory muscles we performed a morphological and immunofluorescence characterization of the diaphragm and pectoralis major muscles. Conclusions Our observations suggest that strychnine poisoning profoundly impacts the morphology of diaphragm fibers, with both fast and slow fibers presenting hypercontraction areas. While the accessory respiratory muscle pectoralis major presents milder alterations, with fewer fibers with hypercontraction areas. This work represents the first histological investigation on the impact of strychnine on skeletal muscle fibers, and suggests distinct influence of this poison on diaphragm and pectoralis major muscles.

title: Topical 15% trichloroacetic acid versus silver nitrate cauterization in the management of idiopathic childhood epistaxis: a prospective randomized clinical trial
abstractText: Abstract The purpose of the study is to compare the outcomes of trichloroacetic acid (TCA) to silver nitrate chemical cauterization in managing pediatric epistaxis. In this prospective randomized assessor-blinded clinical trial, of 172 randomized patients, 157 pediatric patients with idiopathic anterior epistaxis were divided into 2 groups in a ratio 1:1, where group (A) was treated with silver nitrate 25% after local anesthesia application and group (B) was treated with 15% TCA locally applied to the bleeder. Patients were assessed upon recurrence, pain, and crusting at 1st, 2nd, 4th, and 12th week post-intervention. The incidence of epistaxis was not significantly different between the two groups. Pain was significantly greater in the TCA group ( P = 0.008*). Nasal crusting was slightly greater in the TCA group, but the difference was not statistically significant. Conclusion : Although not widely utilized in the management of pediatric epistaxis, TCA is considered an effective chemical cautery agent for the management of childhood epistaxis, with results comparable to those of silver nitrate in terms of recurrence but was slightly worse in terms of pain after intervention. Trial Registration : Number NCT06836791, Date of registration 02/19/2025. What is Known: • Epistaxis is a very distressing complaint in pediatric otorhinolaryngology. • One of the utilized modalities nowadays that proved efficacy in the management of epistaxis is the chemical cauterization of the prominent vessels in Little’s area. What is New: • This is the first study to compare the efficacy of silver nitrate to TCA in epistaxis treatment. • TCA is considered an effective chemical cautery agent for the management of childhood epistaxis, with results comparable to those of silver nitrate agent.

title: Design of an analysis application for predict demand forecasting in inventory system
abstractText: Trading companies often face challenges in managing their inventory systems and finding it hard to match inventory levels with the increasing demand from consumers. This paper tries to create a system that can forecast how much of a product customers might want and also check how well different deep learning methods work. In this paper, the author uses both experimental and applied methods to check how well each deep learning algorithm works.The algorithms tested are CNN-LSTM, LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, and Transformer. The author used data from Kaggle that includes 76,000 sales records from 2022 up to 2024, covering different product categories such as clothing, furniture, electronics, toys, and groceries. The data was then cleaned and split into groups for training and testing. The author found the results by testing various deep learning algorithms. The top performing algorithm is CNN-LSTM, which has MAE of 28.2136, RMSE of 36.6037, and R² of 0.3106. Even though the R2 value shows the model doesn't have strong predictive power yet, it is still the best performing model out of all the ones studied in this research. By comparing the system's performance to standard operating levels, it was found that the system can adjust to changes in demand.This suggests it could help trading companies better manage their stock and offer more understanding of how deep learning models work.

title: ANALISIS AWAL MINAT BELAJAR DAN KETERAMPILAN GERAK TARI TRADISIONAL SISWA KELAS V.A SDN 1 MUARA BELITI
abstractText: ABSTRACT Learning interest is one of the factors associated with students' engagement in the learning process, including traditional dance education. This study aimed to describe the initial conditions of students' learning interest and traditional dance movement skills and to analyze the relationship between these two variables among fifth-grade students of class V.A at SDN 1 Muara Beliti. This research employed a descriptive quantitative approach involving 21 students based on the available pretest data. Data were collected through measurements of learning interest and dance movement skills and analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation. The results showed that the learning interest variable had a total score of 361, a mean of 17.19, a median of 14, and a standard deviation of 7.45, with observed scores ranging from 10 to 30. Meanwhile, the traditional dance movement skills variable had a total score of 238, a mean of 11.33, a median of 9, and a standard deviation of 4.19, with observed scores ranging from 8 to 22. Pearson correlation analysis revealed a strong and statistically significant positive relationship between learning interest and traditional dance movement skills (r = 0.903; p < 0.001). This finding indicates that students with higher learning interest scores tend to achieve higher traditional dance movement skills scores. Therefore, learning interest is strongly associated with students' traditional dance movement skills. However, these findings are limited to the initial conditions of a single class and cannot establish a causal relationship or demonstrate the effectiveness of the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model. ABSTRAK Minat belajar merupakan salah satu faktor yang berkaitan dengan keterlibatan siswa dalam mengikuti pembelajaran, termasuk pembelajaran seni tari tradisional. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan kondisi awal minat belajar dan keterampilan gerak tari tradisional serta menganalisis hubungan antara kedua variabel tersebut pada siswa kelas V.A SDN 1 Muara Beliti. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif dengan melibatkan 21 siswa berdasarkan data awal (pretest) yang tersedia. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui pengukuran minat belajar dan keterampilan gerak tari, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif dan korelasi Pearson. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa variabel minat belajar memperoleh skor total 361, rata-rata 17,19, median 14, dan simpangan baku 7,45, dengan rentang skor 10–30. Sementara itu, variabel keterampilan gerak tari memperoleh skor total 238, rata-rata 11,33, median 9, dan simpangan baku 4,19, dengan rentang skor 8–22. Hasil uji korelasi Pearson menunjukkan adanya hubungan positif yang kuat dan signifikan antara minat belajar dan keterampilan gerak tari tradisional (r = 0,903; p < 0,001). Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa semakin tinggi skor minat belajar siswa, cenderung semakin tinggi pula skor keterampilan gerak tari yang diperoleh. Dengan demikian, minat belajar memiliki keterkaitan yang kuat dengan keterampilan gerak tari tradisional. Namun, temuan ini terbatas pada gambaran kondisi awal satu kelas dan belum dapat digunakan untuk menyimpulkan hubungan sebab-akibat maupun efektivitas model Project-Based Learning (PjBL).

title: Printable Monolayer of Binary Polymer-Co-Grafted Au Nanoparticles for Nano-Floating-Gate Transistor Memory
abstractText: Abstract Nano-floating-gate organic field-effect transistor (NFGOFET) memories are promising candidates for flexible, low-cost, and solution-processable nonvolatile memory devices. Their performance relies critically on the construction of a uniform nano-floating-gate/tunneling-dielectric (NFG/TD) layer, in which discrete nanoparticles serve as charge-storage sites and the surrounding polymer matrix functions as the tunneling dielectric. However, the solution processing of the upper organic semiconductor layer often causes solvent-induced erosion of polymer tunneling layers, disrupting the nanoparticle distribution and degrading charge transport and storage. Here, we report a solvent-resistant NFG/TD layer based on binary polymer-co-modified gold nanoparticles and in situ SiO2 interfacial engineering. Gold nanoparticles co-grafted with polystyrene and poly(4-vinylpyridine) form a printable monolayer in which polystyrene serves as the tunneling dielectric and poly(4-vinylpyridine) provides anchoring sites for TEOS hydrolysis. The SiO2 layer preserves the nanoparticle monolayer during active-layer printing and provides a stable inorganic tunneling barrier and a modifiable interface for improving semiconductor crystallization. This work establishes a general and scalable interfacial regulation strategy for the solution-process of printable multi-layered organic thin-film devices.

Fuel treatment efficacy and longevity: regional trends and drivers
abstractText: Background Understanding the drivers of fuel treatment effectiveness and longevity will help land managers strategically apply and maintain treatments. Aims To assess the relative importance of climate and weather (top-down factors) and vegetation and topography (bottom-up factors) in fuel treatment effectiveness. Methods We used climate, weather, vegetation, and topographic variables with the Fuel Treatment Effectiveness Monitoring database to assess fuel treatment effectiveness in California, USA. Machine learning models assessed the relative importance of these factors. Scenario analyses investigated treatment longevity. Key results Modelled fuel treatment effectiveness showed no marked decline over the first 10 years after treatment when controlling for treatment and vegetation types, topography, climate, and weather. Climate and weather helped predict successful modification of fire behaviour, whereas topography helped identify conditions associated with failure. Conclusions Fuel treatment effectiveness can be enhanced by carefully considering vegetation type, topography, and treatment size. Implications As warming and drying trends alter fire weather conditions, managers can use the vegetation, topographic, and treatment-size factors identified here to plan future fuel treatments.
